extraction.name: CIFAR-10
extraction.description: A dataset of 60,000 32x32 color images labeled as one of ten classes, divided into 50,000 training images and 10,000 validation images.
extraction.creator: Krizhevsky et al.
extraction.citeAs: Jordan, Keller. 94% on CIFAR-10 in 3.29 Seconds on a Single GPU. arXiv:2404.00498v2, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 32x32 color images labeled into ten classes.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is divided into a training set of 50,000 images and a validation set of 10,000 images.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Training uses random horizontal flipping and 2-pixel random translation with reflection padding; evaluation uses horizontal flipping and multi-crop test-time augmentation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each image is labeled as one of ten classes.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset facilitates thousands of research projects per year, and faster training on it can accelerate research and reduce experiment costs.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The methods were developed solely to maximize training speed on CIFAR-10 under fixed performance and hardware constraints. The proposed alternating flip augmentation improved performance except in training scenarios that did not benefit from horizontal flipping at all; the standard ImageNet trainings considered did not significantly benefit from horizontal flipping. The compiled version has a downside that the one-time compilation process can take several minutes before training runs can begin, so it is only beneficial when many runs are executed at once.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation/testing of machine learning models, especially for CIFAR-10 research projects and benchmarking training speed and accuracy.
